'''Hiranmay Sen Gupta''', {{langx|bn|হিরন্ময় সেন গুপ্ত}}, (1 August 1934 – 8 January 2022) was a Bangladeshi physicist who specialised in [[nuclear physics]].<ref name="Nuclear Physicist">{{cite web|last=Sen Gupta|first=H. M.|title=Microsoft Academic Search|url=http://academic.research.microsoft.com/Author/11418493/h-m-sen-gupta|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160528191253/http://academic.research.microsoft.com/Author/11418493/h-m-sen-gupta|archive-date=28 May 2016|accessdate=30 January 2014}}</ref> In a career spanning five decades he published over 200 research papers and was made a fellow of [[Bangladesh Academy of Sciences]] in 1977.<ref name=bas>{{cite web |url=http://www.bas.org.bd/fellowship/list-of-fellows-/userprofile/hms.html |title=Professor H.M. Sen Gupta |accessdate=30 January 2014 |last=Sen Gupta |first=H. M. |archive-date=2 February 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202174512/http://www.bas.org.bd/fellowship/list-of-fellows-/userprofile/hms.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Biography==
Sen Gupta was born on 1 August 1934 in [[Barisal]] in the then [[Bengal Presidency]] of [[British India]] to Suruchi Bala and Jitendra Nath Sen Gupta.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Fellow Details - Bangladesh Academy of Sciences|url=https://mcdtest.bol-online.com/bas/fellow-details/28|access-date=8 January 2022|website=mcdtest.bol-online.com|archive-date=8 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220108203521/https://mcdtest.bol-online.com/bas/fellow-details/28|url-status=dead}}</ref> He obtained his [[Ph.D.]] in [[nuclear physics]] from the [[University of London]] in 1963, under the supervision of [[Joseph Rotblat]].<ref name=bas/> His doctoral thesis studied the [[Helium atom scattering|scattering of Helium-3 particles]].<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=The scattering of 3He particles of various energies by C, N, O, A and I|url=https://catalogue.libraries.london.ac.uk/record=b2999602~S16|first=H.|last=Sen Gupta}}</ref> He stayed back in the United Kingdom conducting his postdoctoral research at the [[Nuclear Physics Laboratory]] at the [[University of Oxford]] between 1973 and 1976, and at the Department of Physics, [[University of Birmingham]] between 1981 and 1982.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Nuclear physicist Hiranmay Sen Gupta dies|url=https://thefinancialexpress.com.bd/national/nuclear-physicist-hiranmay-sen-gupta-dies-1641641537|access-date=8 January 2022|website=The Financial Express|language=en}}</ref>

He served as the professor of physics at the [[University of Dhaka]] between 1955 and 2000, where he had also served as the chairman of the department. He was also a senior associate at [[Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] ([[ICTP]]) in [[Trieste]] during 1982 and 1992.<ref name=bas/> He was also a visiting professor at the [[Kyushu University]] in [[Fukuoka, Japan]] in 1994.<ref name=":1" /> He retired in 2000.<ref name=":0" /> In a career spanning five decades he published over 200 research papers and was a fellow of [[Bangladesh Academy of Sciences]] since 1977.<ref name=":0" /> His research interests included [[condensed matter theory]] specializing in the study of [[Elastic scattering|elastic]] and [[inelastic scattering]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Sa-yakanit|first=Virulh|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cPLFCgAAQBAJ&dq=H+M+Sen+Gupta&pg=PA420|title=Condensed Matter Theories, Volume 23 - Proceedings Of The 31st International Workshop|date=4 December 2008|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-4469-37-1|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=H. M. Sen Gupta's research works {{!}} University of Dhaka, Dhaka and other places|url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/H-M-Sen-Gupta-73184958|access-date=2022-01-09|website=ResearchGate|language=en}}</ref> His book in [[Bangla Language|Bangla]] on nuclear physics, published by University of Dhaka, was part of the curriculum for [[MSc]] and [[MPhil]] students at the university.<ref name=":1" />

Sen Gupta died in [[Dhaka]] at the BIRDEM General Hospital on 8 January 2022, at the age of 87.<ref>[https://thefinancialexpress.com.bd/national/nuclear-physicist-hiranmay-sen-gupta-dies-1641641537 Nuclear physicist Hiranmay Sen Gupta dies]</ref> He was married and had two sons.<ref name=":0" />

==Awards==
* H.P. Roy Gold Medal (1967)<ref name=":1" />
* A. Rob Chowdhury Gold Medal (1975)<ref name=":1" />
* Sonali Bank Gold Medal (1984)
* Ibrahim Gold Medal (1992)<ref name=bas/>
